---
title: "Bet selection: three families of rule, and where the edge is not"
subtitle: "Paper 6 in a series on UK All-Weather racing outcomes"
author: "Patrick Gillen"
date: "2026-09-10"
abstract: |
  A betting rule has three independent parts: which horse to back, which
  races to bet on the strength of the model's own output, and which races to
  bet on the strength of the race itself. Two earlier rounds of this work
  searched the first two and concluded that nothing beat the rule paper 1
  inherited from Owen. This paper adds the third — filters on field size,
  class, course, distance and going, all known the night before the race —
  and puts every candidate in all three families through a stability guard
  before anything reaches the test split: a rule must rank in the top decile
  of its family on both halves of the search window to be carried forward.
  The guard struck Owen's rule on three of the four markets, which is a fact
  about that rule worth recording. It did not save the search. One rule won
  every search-set leaderboard — back the horse whose model probability most
  exceeds its market probability, in fields of eleven to twelve runners —
  returning
  `r local({ S <- file.path(rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj")), "_targets_p6"); d <- targets::tar_read(p6_round3_ranks, store = S)$table; r <- d[d$bet == "win" & d$rule == "P4 / field size 11-12", ]; sprintf("%+.1f%%", 100 * r$val_roi) })`
  on the win market with the two halves of the window agreeing to within two
  points, and
  `r local({ S <- file.path(rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj")), "_targets_p6"); d <- targets::tar_read(p6_round3_ranks, store = S)$table; r <- d[d$bet == "win" & d$rule == "P4 / field size 11-12", ]; sprintf("%+.1f%%", 100 * r$test_roi) })`
  on the test split. Search-set rank predicts test rank *negatively* on all
  four markets. Across the threshold family, two thirds to four fifths of the
  variation in return between rules is explained by the mean price the rule
  backs, so a leaderboard mostly ranks price bands; the residual is not
  stable across halves of the same window. The two best rules on the test
  split were the two carried forward without being selected: the market
  favourite in every race, with no model in it, and Owen's rule. Three rules
  in the whole shortlist are profitable once the bookmaker's margin is
  removed and none is profitable with it in place. Since paper 4 showed the
  model ties the settled starting price and beats the overnight forecast
  price, its value sits between the two — and every backtest in this series
  settles at the closing end of that interval, the one price where the answer
  was already known to be no.
format:
  html: default
  pdf:
    toc: true
    number-sections: true
bibliography: references.bib
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(targets)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(glue)

# Paper 6 reads the paper-6 store. Like papers 4 and 5 and unlike papers 1-3
# this does NOT call tar_config_set(): that writes the project-root
# `_targets.yaml`, which papers 1-3's own setup chunks also write, and
# pointing it at `_targets_p6` would send their next render at the wrong
# store. Passing `store =` per call leaves `_targets.yaml` untouched.
P6_ROOT <- rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj"))
P6_STORE <- file.path(P6_ROOT, "_targets_p6")

source(file.path(P6_ROOT, "papers", "06_betting_strategy", "_helpers.R"))

# tar_load() centrally so tarchetypes::tar_quarto() picks these up as render
# dependencies — files pulled in via {{< include >}} are not auto-scanned.
tar_load(c(
  # universe, gates, provenance
  p6_universe, p6_search_set_check, p6_fit_provenance_tbl, p6_ledger_gate,
  p6_sweep_gate, p6_round3_gate,
  # what was searched (_01)
  p6_explore_bets, p6_explore_grid, p6_rc_all_specs, p6_rc_pruned,
  p6_rc_kept, p6_rc_terciles, p6_agree_max, p6_agree_owen,
  # what was found (_02)
  p6_val_sweep, p6_rc_sweep_full, p6_comb_sweep_full, p6_rc_best_pairs,
  p6_rc_guard, p6_thr_guard, p6_comb_guard, p6_guard_summary,
  p6_guard_summary_sub, p6_owen_guard, p6_round3_shortlists,
  p6_round3_val, p6_round3_test, p6_round3_ranks, p6_explore_ranks,
  # price band (_03)
  p6_price_band_fit, p6_price_context,
  # staking (_04)
  p6_staking_test, p6_staking_val, p6_stage3_rules,
  # descriptive
  p6_field_sizes_val, p6_field_sizes_test, p6_overround_val,
  p6_eachway_terms_decision
), store = P6_STORE)

BET_LAB <- p6_bet_labels()
```
